All separating sets of a pair of responses

Source: R/cpdag.R
mc_separating_sets.Rd

Enumerates every conditioning set that makes a pair of responses conditionally uncorrelated at the second order, given a skeleton. The skeleton search of mc_pc_skeleton stops at the first such set and records only that one, which is all the standard v-structure rule needs. The order-independent orientation rules need the whole collection, and they need it on the final skeleton rather than on the neighborhoods that happened to be live when the edge was deleted, so it is rebuilt here from scratch: for the pair \((i, j)\) every subset of the neighbors of \(i\) other than \(j\), and every subset of the neighbors of \(j\) other than \(i\), of size at most max_ord, is tested, and the separating ones are returned. A set reachable from both neighborhoods is reported once.

Usage

mc_separating_sets(
  Sigma,
  n,
  adjacency,
  pairs = NULL,
  alpha = 0.05,
  max_ord = NULL,
  df_residual = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'mcg_sepsets'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

Sigma

an \(R \times R\) covariance matrix of the responses.

n

number of experimental units, taken as independent; the test is the one of mc_pc_skeleton, with the same clamp of the partial correlation and no cluster argument.

adjacency

the symmetric 0/1 skeleton, for instance the adjacency component of mc_pc_skeleton.

pairs

optional integer matrix with two columns giving the pairs to examine; NULL takes every non-adjacent pair. The pairs must be non-adjacent in adjacency, since a separating set is not defined for an edge of the skeleton.

alpha

significance level of the conditional-association test, on the same contract as mc_pc_skeleton.

max_ord

largest conditioning set enumerated; NULL uses \(R - 2\).

df_residual

optional residual degrees of freedom \(\nu_e\) of the first-stage fit, a number or the result of mc_residual_df, passed to the same Fisher contract used by the skeleton.

x

an object of class "mcg_sepsets".

...

ignored.

Value

An object of class "mcg_sepsets": a list with pairs (one row per pair examined, with the number of separating sets found and a truncated flag), sets (one row per separating set, with its label, size, partial correlation and p-value), the 0/1 matrix members of set membership, and diagnostics. The truncated flag of a pair is TRUE when its collection may be incomplete: a neighborhood of the pair is larger than max_ord, or some conditioning set gave no valid test, because its Fisher degrees of freedom are not positive or its block gives no valid partial correlation. Such a set is skipped and counted in n_unusable; unlike in mc_pc_skeleton, it does not stop the enumeration. The object also records alpha, max_ord, df_residual and response_names, and diagnostics with the number of tests (n_tests), of ridge-regularized blocks (n_regularized), of unusable blocks (n_unusable), the largest ridge (max_ridge) and the Fisher contract (df_contract). The print method returns x invisibly.

Why the collection is informative on its own

Two sets can separate the same pair with very different strength, and the skeleton keeps whichever the enumeration reached first. Reporting the collection shows how much of the orientation rests on that arbitrary choice.

References

Ramsey, J., Zhang, J. and Spirtes, P. (2006). Adjacency-faithfulness and conservative causal inference. Proceedings of the 22nd Conference on Uncertainty in Artificial Intelligence, 401-408.

Colombo, D. and Maathuis, M. H. (2014). Order-independent constraint-based causal structure learning. Journal of Machine Learning Research 15, 3921-3962.

See also

mc_graph_pipeline, whose orient_rule argument consumes this object.

Other structure discovery: mc_find_vstructures(), mc_ges(), mc_graph_pipeline(), mc_orient_meek(), mc_pc_skeleton(), mc_residual_df(), mc_skeleton_to_bnlearn()

Examples

set.seed(1); n <- 600
z1 <- rnorm(n); z2 <- rnorm(n); z3 <- 0.7 * z1 + 0.7 * z2 + rnorm(n)
S <- cov(cbind(z1, z2, z3))
sk <- mc_pc_skeleton(S, n)
mc_separating_sets(S, n, sk$adjacency)$sets
#>   pair i j response1 response2 set size       pcor   p_value
#> 1    1 1 2        z1        z2  {}    0 0.03853124 0.3462323
